dimensionClassifications.meaning: A named system axis intentionally selectable by a product or user.
Computed from typed foundation, semantic roles, recipe, or runtime preferences.
A stable system obligation whose meaning must not vary by route.

controlMeasure.note: A control chooses a named measure; it does not author a pixel width.

collectionMeasure.note: A collection may choose content or wide measure; item geometry remains component-owned.

touchTarget.note: The minimum touch target is a shared system obligation across Web and native renderers.

stateColor.note: Invalid, disabled, selected, and status colors resolve from semantic roles and never from route literals.

profileChoice.note: Profiles select named recipe, density, and approved brand aliases; they do not fork input components.

oneOffArrangement.note: A one-off arrangement can remain local when it has no system-wide reuse obligation.

ownership.webProjection: buildThemeVariables -> CSS custom properties consumed by the Web renderer
ownership.nativeProjection: buildNativeThemeSnapshot -> typed JS/TS values consumed by a future native renderer
ownership.aiProjection: generated input-contracts.json and inputContract fields on component shards

label.note: The label names the control; required or optional indication is supplementary text.

description.note: Helper content is associated through aria-describedby or the equivalent renderer relationship.

error.note: Validation copy is associated with the invalid control and is not represented by color alone.

action.note: Actions remain explicit controls owned by the consumer and are ordered after the affected fields.

formStates.disabled: Prevents interaction, remains discoverable, and exposes disabled-state semantics.
formStates.readOnly: Keeps the value and accessible name available while preventing mutation.
formStates.invalid: Exposes the invalid state and an associated explanation; no color-only error contract.
formStates.loading: Communicates pending work and prevents duplicate activation where applicable.
formStates.empty: Communicates an empty value or result set without treating absence as a rendering failure.
formStates.error: Communicates a failed or rejected operation with recovery guidance when the consumer can provide it.
formStates.virtualKeyboard: Keeps the active field, label, error, and primary action usable when the viewport is reduced.

date.timezone: consumer-owned; the control stores a date value without timezone conversion

time.timezone: consumer-owned; the control stores a local wall-clock value

range.ordering: the component normalizes the selected range order; business period meaning stays with the consumer

dateTime.shape: date plus time values composed from DatePicker and TimePicker

fileMetadata.ownership: The renderer selects or presents metadata; the consumer owns transport, persistence, authorization, and retention.

compact.name: compact
compact.note: The smallest generally useful bounded item; it may shrink below its minimum only when the containing surface itself is narrower.

control.name: control
control.note: The default focused-control measure; fields remain fluid below the maximum.

content.name: content
content.note: A bounded content well that preserves useful line length and leaves shell gutters available.

wide.name: wide
wide.note: A wide bounded surface; it does not authorize a universal full-bleed layout.

reading.name: reading
reading.note: Reading is a text measure. Existing recipe rails may retain a ch-based Web projection while native consumes this numeric semantic bound.

fluid.name: fluid
avoidFor: a replacement for a content rail
fluid.note: Fill is an explicit opt-in; it does not change the owning shell or create a new max-width policy.

TreeSelect.reason: A tree-shaped selection is already owned by HierarchyPicker; a path-shaped selection is owned by Cascader.
TreeSelect.aiGuidance: Choose HierarchyPicker for nested node selection and Cascader for one final path leaf.

DateInput.reason: Direct date text entry is already the input half of DatePicker; a separate public identity would duplicate the value and validation boundary.
DateInput.aiGuidance: Use DatePicker for a date field; revisit a separate DateInput only if a distinct parsing or validation contract is approved.

FileInput.reason: FileUpload owns the one authoritative trigger and hidden browser input; exposing FileInput would create a competing file-selection API.
FileInput.aiGuidance: Use FileUpload for selection and pass accepted File metadata to consumer-owned transport.

Dropzone.reason: Dropzone is a Web presentation behavior inside FileUpload, not a separate cross-platform selection intent.
Dropzone.aiGuidance: Use FileUpload; do not create a mobile dropzone. The native renderer maps the same intent to a picker or camera source.

UploadQueue.reason: Queue transport, retry, cancellation, and persistence belong to the consumer or an approved engine; FileList and FileItem remain the presentation boundary.
UploadQueue.aiGuidance: Compose FileList/FileItem with consumer-owned transport state; do not add network behavior to the UI package.

Signature.reason: Capture, stroke smoothing, persistence, and consent semantics require an approved drawing/signature engine and product policy.
Signature.aiGuidance: Defer until an engine adapter and signature-consent contract are approved; do not implement a canvas in a consumer route.

DocumentPicker.note: Native source metadata only; the future renderer chooses the platform document provider and reports cancellation or permission failure.

ImagePicker.note: Native photo-library source metadata only; no image storage or upload behavior is owned here.

CameraCapture.note: Native camera source metadata only; capability, permission, cancellation, and capture failure remain explicit states.

compatibility.existingCatalog: packages/ai/catalog/components.json remains the legacy Web API compatibility surface.
compatibility.existingPlatform: U03 component-platform resolver remains the platform classification authority for implemented catalog entries.
compatibility.variants: NativeSelect and NativeTimeInput are renderer-level variants; aliases and variants do not create a new semantic input intent.
compatibility.consumerBoundary: Consumers own business data, validation rules, permissions, persistence, transport, routing, and native capability policy.
compatibility.noNativePackage: U05 adds no native component package and no React Native dependency.
